newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends up, prices consolidate after data.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends up, prices consolidate after data.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures finished firmer on trade buying that remained light in the wake of Friday's surprise supply and demand data, floor sources said.
"This market couldn't go anywhere today," a trader said. He pegged resistance at 75.00 cents a lb for December delivery and cited a gap on the charts between 73.75 to 75.16.

Prices are more likely to trade sideways to lower, market sources said, based on the USDA's supply and demand report. USDA expects ending stocks and world production to rise while exports and demand will probably remain weak.
"We still have a lot of unsold cotton around," a dealer said. "A light percentage of the crop was forward contracted and there is not enough export business to get thins fired up."
December ended up 0.23 at 73.42, having ranged from 73.78 to 73.16. The back months closed 0.5 higher to 0.05 lower.
Support was seen at 70.00 in December.
